analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md (documentation). The patch hunks (base ~958-962, ~1035-1042; head 961-963, 1041-1056) fall beyond the supplied head units, which cover lines 1-803 and show unchanged surrounding text. The visible units therefore do not include the changed lines. Per the patch excerpt, the changes document (a) a 15-second per-model unload wait at shutdown, with a model whose native retirement never finishes left to process exit (ProviderLoop.unloadAllModelsForShutdown), and (b) a status line for a configuration change that needs a restart, driven by enabled_models_at_start and enabled_models_at_last_switch. These are descriptive and add no code or control change. The documented bounded unload wait is an availability-oriented lifecycle behavior; it relates to T-029 and T-028 (residual GPU memory) only loosely. No security control is weakened in the supplied evidence. I read the visible lines (logout revocation, enrollment, switch, cache) for text that contradicts the threat model: logout still stops the process, revokes at the recorded issuer and confirms only on HTTP 204, matching A-008/T-053. The cache section keeps the encrypted-SSD default and the kill switch, and states that its checks do not certify disk firmware, consistent with T-041. Uncertainty remains on two points: the patch excerpt is truncated, so the exact new status text is unseen, and the underlying source (unloadAllModelsForShutdown) is not supplied, so the claim that a stuck model is left to process exit is unverified. Since a doc-only change cannot itself regress controls, no finding is raised, but the shutdown behavior's effect on residual-data purge (T-028) belongs to whichever PR changes the code.
